Why this mattersSigned in, your documents and settings sync to your account automatically. Signed out, everything lives only in this browser — and opening a new version of this file starts with empty storage (browsers isolate it per file). Back up all data now and then, and before switching files, then Restore right after to carry your data over: it's the only copy outside the browser.

Provider
AI Mode
Sakura Hosted AI uses Sakura's own AI credentials — no key to find or paste, and no separate account with a provider. Requires signing in; each signed-in account gets a daily request quota. A real escape hatch still exists if you'd rather not sign in or want unlimited usage on your own dime: switch to "Bring your own key" above instead. Disclosure: when you use this mode, the text for that request (a node or selected nodes, highlighted text, a note, remark or To-Do line, or the topic you give Generate outline — depending on the feature) is sent to Sakura's server and forwarded to a third-party AI provider Sakura selects — not stored on Sakura's server either way. See Settings → About → Privacy & data for the full picture.
Sakura Hosted AI
Sign in to start using hosted AI — no API key needed.
Provider
▾
All seven built-in providers require their own API key — select one from the Provider dropdown above to see where to get it. GitHub Models requires a fine-grained personal access token with models:read scope. This is a fixed list — Sakura doesn't support adding another API endpoint, so a Content-Security-Policy can restrict outbound requests to these known providers rather than staying open to anywhere. Would rather skip finding a key entirely? Switch to "Sakura Hosted AI" above instead — just sign in.

API Key
No key saved. No requests to this provider yet today.
Fallback orderWhen any error occurs on the active provider (quota, rate limit, or other failure), Sakura retries with the next checked provider in order. The active provider is always tried first. Providers without a saved key are skipped. A toast confirms which provider was used.
Reset AI settingsRestores your provider and model choices to their defaults and clears every saved API key. Also resets the shared rewrite prompt (want just that, without touching your keys? Use "Reset to default" next to the prompt box instead, in Rewrite below). Separate from the general settings reset — your documents and other app preferences aren't touched either way.
Rewrite
Rewrite max response lengthCaps output tokens for the Rewrite feature specifically. Generate Outline uses its own larger cap (2048) and isn't affected by this. Raise this if rewriting a long selection gets cut off.
Rewrite prompt
Auto-rewrite on commit
Auto-rewrite on commitRuns Rewrite automatically on nodes as you finish editing them — no manual click. Queued and sent as a single batched request after two minutes without further edits, or as soon as five nodes have queued up — not one request per node, to avoid burning through provider rate limits during continuous note-taking. Short nodes (under five words), checkbox items, headings, and text containing [[backlinks]] or `code` are left alone. Uses the same Rewrite prompt configured above — there's no separate prompt for auto-rewrite. Requires a usable active provider — an API key configured above for a BYOK provider, or just being signed in for Sakura Hosted AI; if that's not the case right now (no key set, Secure Storage is locked, or hosted is selected and you're signed out), queued nodes wait rather than being discarded and send automatically as soon as the provider becomes usable again. Turns itself off after repeated AI-call failures rather than retrying silently forever — a separate case from simply not having a key yet. Shows a live status in the bottom status bar whenever it's on — how many nodes are queued and when they'll be sent.

About
Sakura
A knowledge-management workspace for structured documents and everyday personal productivity — To-Dos in the Hub.
Single-file, no build step, works offline once loaded, no account required — sign in (Google or email) if you want your documents to follow you across devices, and use optional AI features (rewrite, expand, outline generation, diagram generation, action-item extraction, tagging, and more) with a provider of your choice.

Privacy & data
Everything is stored locally in your browser by default — nothing leaves this tab unless you turn on one of the following.
AI features send the relevant text (a node or selected nodes, highlighted text, a note, remark or To-Do line, or the topic you give Generate outline — depending on the feature) to an AI provider; and signing in (Google or email) syncs your documents and settings to Sakura's own cloud storage so they follow you across devices. Each of these only happens while connected, and only when you actually use that feature.
Which AI provider depends on which mode you've picked in Settings → AI → Provider. With your own API key (the seven built-in providers), that text goes directly from your browser to the provider you configured, using your own key and account — Sakura's own server is never involved. With Sakura Hosted AI, that text instead goes to Sakura's own server first, which forwards it to a third-party provider Sakura selects (currently Groq, Cerebras, or Gemini) using Sakura's own credentials, and returns the response — Sakura's server doesn't store that text either way, only a per-day request count against your account's quota.
An account holds your documents, folders, To-Dos and app settings — and nothing else. No analytics or tracking anywhere in Sakura, and other users can never access your data.
Signing in with Google only shares your name, email, and profile picture — the same info shown in the account menu, not stored anywhere beyond that. Email sign-in needs only the email and password themselves, handled directly by Firebase Authentication — no separate profile data involved.
