Welcome — where would you like to start?

Pick how you want to get familiar. You can always revisit both from the Help menu.

Sakura

Why an outliner — and why Sakura?

Think of an outliner as turning your notes into a family tree, instead of a messy pile of paragraphs. Instead of writing left to right, you write in points that tuck inside one another. Here's why that makes life easier:

See the big picture without the clutter Five pages of notes usually means scrolling forever to find what you want. In Sakura, you can collapse the details and see just your main headings — like a table of contents. Click one open when you need it.
Move things around like LEGO blocks In a normal document, moving a section means highlighting, cutting, pasting, and fixing the spacing. Here you just grab one point and drag it — everything tucked underneath comes with it automatically.
Bring in the mess, get back structure Paste in messy notes or import a Word document — Sakura sorts it into a tree for you, AI-assisted when it needs to be. This part's specific to Sakura, not outliners in general.
It keeps you thinking, not just typing Plain note-taking lets you write down what someone said without really processing it. An outliner makes you decide, in the moment: is this a new idea, or a detail under the last one? That keeps you actively sorting instead of just transcribing.
It grows into a full workspace, not just a tree Attach notes, questions and answers, remarks, tables, or a real embedded diagram to any node, then export the whole thing as a PDF. Track to-dos alongside it. All still the same outline underneath — nothing here is a separate app bolted on.
Not every kind of writing wants this. Flowing essays and loosely connected notes are still better off elsewhere — Sakura's built for things that have a shape: plans, specs, architecture, meeting notes, decisions.

Section icon library

These are the only emoji that get swapped for a matching SVG line icon on section-header rows. Anything not shown here stays as plain emoji — that's the mix "Render section icons as SVG" warns about.

Sakura Cheatsheet

Everything at a glance — full detail lives in Help
No matching shortcuts

The Basics

  • Enter/F2 edit node
  • Enter new sibling (while editing)
  • Shift+Enter split at cursor
  • new child
  • Tab/Shift+Tab indent / outdent
  • / move node
  • ←/→ collapse / expand
  • Click select · Shift+click range · Ctrl/Cmd+click multi
  • Right-click → icon row (Rewrite, Note, Thread, Add diagram, Add table, Add image) + More for insert above/below, duplicate, move, sort, delete, and everything else

Semantics

  • **Text** → bold (or select text + Ctrl/Cmd+B)
  • __Text__ → italic (or select text + Ctrl/Cmd+I)
  • @Node name → clickable backlink (type @ while editing to pick)
  • [ ] text or [x] text → auto-converts to checkbox on commit
  • Outline numbering — Settings → Editing → "Outline numbering" (1, 1.1, 1.1.1)

Formatting

  • bold
  • italic
  • underline
  • strike
  • highlight
  • text color
  • –6 heading 1–6 (independent of depth)
  • [Text] → Section · (Text) → note
  • !Text → alert · `Text` → code
  • @Node name → backlink (type @ while editing to pick)
  • [ ] or [x] at start → auto-converts to checkbox on commit

Tables

  • Tab/Shift+Tab next / previous cell (Tab in the last cell adds a row)
  • Enter cell below (in the last row, adds a row)
  • Shift+Enter new line inside the cell
  • ↑/↓ cell above / below from a cell's first / last line
  • Esc finish editing the table
  • Ctrl/Cmd+V paste a spreadsheet range into the cells
  • Add table… size picker: arrows choose, Enter inserts, Esc cancels

Toolbar

  • Undo / Redo — /
  • Add child —
  • Select all —
  • Bold, italic, highlight, text color, heading style — text styling (underline , strikethrough )
  • Collapse / Expand all — or ▶ button
  • Paste indented or bulleted text — Ctrl/Cmd+V parses it into nodes
  • Insert date/time —
  • Note —

Search & Quick Assist

  • Quick Assist — plain-English commands, or search anything
  • Quick Insert — a small character-insert menu (em dash, en dash, arrow, check mark, cross mark, middle dot, date/time), the same everywhere you're editing text — see Quick Insert below
  • Covers settings, help, doc names, node text, notes, tags, discussion items (remarks and questions), diagrams, tables and image captions — across all documents
  • Results group by type ("In documents", "Notes", "Tags", "Discussion") with a snippet — click to jump straight there
  • search this tree
  • search & replace
  • File Explorer filter only matches doc names — use header search for text inside docs

Notes & inline objects

  • Note — per-node, rich text ·
  • Thread — add to the row's conversation ·
  • Floating, draggable, to expand full-screen
  • Notes: B I U S, lists, link, table, image paste, AI rewrite
  • Right-click a node → Thread… / Add diagram… — each lives inline under that node (comments and questions share the node's one thread; Enter adds an entry, the row marker and the thread status move together); click the node's dot to show or hide them
  • Paste or drop a screenshot on a node (or right-click → Add image…) — thumbnails under the node; click one to enlarge, caption, or resize for the PDF
  • M in the image viewer: Mark up — rectangle R, arrow A, highlighter H, text T, select/move V
  • Diagrams — a real draw.io editor per diagram, linked to a node; embeds as a picture in PDF exports. Right-click → Generate diagram drafts one from a branch

To-Dos

  • App-level task list — not tied to any document or node ·
  • Floating, draggable, to expand full-screen
  • Check off a task to move it to Completed (newest first); turn on the select/reorder toggle to drag-reorder Open tasks
  • Priority and due-date chips below each task; both auto-hide until set or hovered.
  • A task can repeat (Daily/Weekdays/Weekly — completing it just advances the due date) or hold sub-tasks (nested checklist, parent auto-completes when all are checked) — not both at once
  • Right-click a task for a context menu — duplicate, copy text, move to top/bottom, expand/collapse sub-tasks, delete
  • Type @ in task text for inline chips, with autocomplete — @name assignee, @date (e.g. @tomorrow, @fri), @status (waiting/blocked/done/review) — display only
  • # for a #tag (autocompletes from prior tags), > for a muted remark to end of line — both display only
  • Quick-find matches #tags, @mentions, and remark text too — it's a plain substring search over the task text
  • Filter by priority, status, and due date at once (Overdue/Today/Due later/No due date) — all three combine, and the filter menu stays open so you can set several before closing it
  • The same toggle also reveals each task's drag handle. Select multiple open tasks to bulk-set priority, status, or due date, or bulk-complete/delete — each with its own Undo, same as the single-task actions
  • Settings → To-Dos: auto-expiry and a cap on completed tasks
  • Searchable from Quick Assist — plain text or todo: milk

AI Features

  • Rewrite — selected node(s), or highlighted text
  • Generate outline ·
  • Batches over 30 nodes send in sequential chunks
  • Settings → AI → AI Mode: "Sakura Hosted AI" (sign in, zero setup) or "Bring your own key" (seven built-in providers — Gemini, Groq, Claude, ChatGPT, OpenRouter, Cerebras, GitHub Models — paste your own API key) — all AI features share whichever is active

Copy & Export

  • copy selected nodes — paste back into any Sakura document, or into another app as text
  • Export ▾ → PDF .pdf — renders the full document, always fully expanded
  • Export ▾ → OPML .opml — outline structure, text, and notes; always includes folded sections
  • Import ▾ in header — OPML file, as a new document
  • File Explorer footer → Backup / Restore — full app data

Docs, Tabs & Zen

  • new document
  • Click a doc's icon in the file explorer → pick from a small icon set
  • close tab
  • save now
  • toggle zen mode
  • Esc exit zen mode only (doesn't toggle back in)

Optional capabilities

  • AI Capabilities (Settings → AI) — Generate outline, Rewrite, Auto-rewrite
  • @ Mentions & Backlinks (Settings → Panels) — link nodes; type @ to mention another by name
  • Focus (Settings → Editing) — zoom into a branch; Ctrl/Cmd + . to enter, Ctrl/Cmd + , to exit
  • Off = hidden, not deleted — data is always preserved; states saved across sessions

Tabs

  • Click a doc in the file explorer or + at end of strip → open as tab
  • new document
  • close active tab (doc stays in file explorer)
  • Double-click tab → rename · Drag to reorder · ▾ → search open tabs
  • Each tab keeps its own undo history, scroll, and selection
  • Settings → Startup → "Reopen tabs on launch" restores them next session

Version History

  • Right-click a doc in the file explorer → "Version history" → automatic snapshots
  • Snapshot taken before content would be overwritten — at most once per ~10 min, capped at last 10 per document
  • "Save a version now" → snapshot immediately, useful before a big rewrite
  • Restoring saves current content as a version first — always reversible

Shortcuts

  • Settings → Keyboard Shortcuts → Customize — remap any action
  • save now
  • Quick Assist — commands, or search anything
  • generate outline (AI)
  • Shortcuts blocked by OS/browser always have a matching button
Shortcuts blocked by the OS or browser always have a matching button or menu item that works instead.
